title: Tenstorrent raises $1.5 billion to scale chips for open-weight models
friendlyTitle: Tenstorrent raises $1.5 billion for chips that serve open models
summary: Tenstorrent, a 10-year-old inference-chip company led by Jim Keller, has raised $1.5 billion at a $6.2 billion valuation. TechCrunch says the round was led by Trace Capital and Innovation X, with Cadence Ventures, Eclipse, Fidelity, SanDisk, and T. Rowe Price also in. The valuation is more than double the $2.6 billion from late 2024. Keller told Bloomberg the company stayed independent after showing that its Galaxy servers could run DeepSeek models. The new capital is for chips aimed at serving open-weight models and video generation.

whyItMatters: Open models only help if someone other than Nvidia can serve them at a price a company will pay. This round does not put a new chip on your desk. It does say investors are still funding that alternative, after acquisition interest earlier this year did not end in a sale.
